title: Where you finish is not the whole trip
subtitle: Position, distance, and displacement
paragraphs: If I say a cart is at two meters, you need to know where we started measuring. Position needs a chosen zero, called the origin. We also choose a positive direction. On today's notes page, right is positive. Once those choices are clear, a position tells us where the cart is along the line.

Position is a location. Distance counts how much travel occurred. Displacement describes the change from starting position to final position. Those are three different questions, so one trip can have three different descriptions. I want you to decide which question is being asked before calculating anything.

Trace both legs in Section C. It shows a trip from 0 m to 4 m, then back to 1 m. The outward leg is four meters long. The return leg is three meters long. Total distance is distance = 4 m + 3 m = 7 m. Coming back does not erase the first leg. Distance counts every part of the route and is never negative.

Displacement uses only the starting and finishing positions. The symbol Δ means “change in,” so Δ<var>x</var> means change in position. The rule is <eq>Δ<var>x</var> = <var>x</var><sub>f</sub> − <var>x</var><sub>i</sub></eq>: finish minus start. For the diagram, <eq>Δ<var>x</var> = 1 m − 0 m = +1 m</eq>. The cart finishes one meter right of where it began, even though it traveled seven meters.

Now find the starting and turning positions in Section D. The cart starts at 2 m, travels to 6 m, and returns to 4 m. Its first leg is 6 m − 2 m = 4 m. The return leg has length 6 m − 4 m = 2 m. Add the lengths to find distance = 4 m + 2 m = 6 m. The direction of a leg does not make its length negative.

For displacement, use the endpoints instead: <eq>Δ<var>x</var> = 4 m − 2 m = +2 m</eq>. The final position is 4 m from our chosen zero, while the displacement is 2 m right of the starting point. Those answers differ because the cart did not start at zero. This is a common place to lose track of what a number means.

Distance is a scalar: it has size and units. Displacement is a vector: it also has direction. Along one axis, the sign gives that direction. A negative displacement would mean a finish left of the start. In the diagram, the traveled route stays in pencil; the positions and displacement arrow are blue.

For our fictional asteroid, 2026-XJ, we need the same clear reference frame. Measuring from Earth gives our classroom model a zero, but we must still name the positive direction. Total distance describes the route traveled. Starting position and displacement tell us where the asteroid ends up. That is the information a position forecast needs.

A.title: KEY VOCABULARY
A.text: SECTION A KEY VOCABULARY Position Where are you? Measured from a chosen zero, with a chosen + direction. Distance How much travel? Counts every part of the path. Never negative. Displacement What changed from start to finish? The sign gives the direction. Scalar / vector Distance has size only (scalar). Displacement has size and direction (vector).

B.title: KEY EQUATIONS + UNITS
B.text: SECTION B KEY EQUATIONS + UNITS Δx = x f − x i distance = leg 1 + leg 2 + … Δ “change in” (finish − start) x position, meters (m)

C.title: COLOR IT · ONE TRIP, THREE QUESTIONS
C.text: SECTION C COLOR IT · ONE TRIP, THREE QUESTIONS 0 m → 4 m → 1 m. Right is +. out: 4 m back: 3 m displacement: +1 m 0 1 2 3 4 5 m 1 1 2 3 4 1 · PENCIL Distance: trace both legs 2 · BLUE Displacement arrow 3 · BLUE Start position 4 · BLUE Finish position

D.title: WORKED EXAMPLE
D.text: SECTION D WORKED EXAMPLE A cart goes from 2 m to 6 m, then back to 4 m. Right is positive. Find the distance and the displacement. GIVEN x i = 2 m turn at 6 m x f = 4 m EQUATION distance = leg 1 + leg 2 Δx = x f − x i WORK 4 m + 2 m 4 m − 2 m ANSWER distance 6 m displacement +2 m

E.title: THE 2026-XJ THREAD
E.text: SECTION E THE 2026-XJ THREAD DAY 2 OF 22 · NEW TOOL: A REFERENCE FRAME Before we can say where XJ is, we need a zero and a + direction. Analysts measure its position from Earth and track its displacement, not the winding path it travels. Unit question: How fast is it moving, and where will it arrive?

words.definition: Where are you? Measured from a chosen zero, with a chosen + direction.
How much travel? Counts every part of the path. Never negative.
What changed from start to finish? The sign gives the direction.
Distance has size only (scalar). Displacement has size and direction (vector).
